source_ref: OSF ntrp8 (Sun, Wu & Goodwin 2025, doi:10.1037/pspp0000539): component 9ndt2 Codebook.xlsx (file e5a26, sha256 253413979acb50ff...) sheet 'Study 3', block 'NOMINATOR-REPORTED MORAL RATINGS' (stem and nt.<adjective> labels, scale '1 = Not at all, 5 = Moderately, 9 = Extremely'); component 5e9y3 data-clean/study3-maindat.csv (file wvq64, sha256 e94bec871e1a9c2d...) for the it.* response columns; 5e9y3 analyses.R (file zdk78) lines 218-219 and 5248-5270 (Figure S8); PsyArXiv preprint sd8t4_v1 with supplement (file jc3ru, sha256 be2442ceaaa6a2ae...), Supplemental Figure S8 note; data/sun_2025_morality.do Bookmark #40.
note: CODE DERIVATION: code IS the source column name - study3-maindat.csv header 'it.cruel' etc.; Stata import drops the dot, rename *, lower -> itcruel. Self-describing adjective codes. WORDING: the 30 adjective labels are copied verbatim from Codebook.xlsx sheet 'Study 3', where they are documented against the NOMINATOR variables nt.<adjective> (38 adjectives) under the stem "To what extent is [target's name]…" (codebook's own ellipsis character kept) with anchors 1 = Not at all, 5 = Moderately, 9 = Extremely. The codebook has no rows for the informant it.<adjective> variables. The preprint supplement's Figure S8 ("Correlations Between Other Informant-Reported Traits and General Morality") establishes that informants rated the same adjective set: its note says "We did not collect informant reports of the following adjectives: angry, curious, creative, organized, outgoing, assertive, moody, and insecure" - removing those 8 from the codebook's 38 leaves exactly the 30 live adjectives. So the stem and anchors are carried over from the nominator form of the same study's same adjective battery; the informant form's stem is not separately printed anywhere checked (codebook, main paper, 145-page preprint+supplement, analyses.R). The live resp range 1-9 is consistent with the 1/5/9 scale. Scale points 2,3,4,6,7,8 are unlabelled in the source and left blank. Figure S8's plot labels match the codebook wording (e.g. 'Mean-spirited', 'Socially conscious', 'Self-controlled', 'Physically attractive'); one differs only in hyphenation ('Hard-working' in analyses.R's figure labels vs codebook 'Hardworking') - codebook form shipped. DATA DEFECT 1 (composites): itkindness and itintegrity are NOT items. analyses.R line 218: dat$it.kindness <- rowMeans(dat[,c('it.AGR.C','it.AGR.R')]); line 219: dat$it.integrity <- rowMeans(dat[,c('it.MCQ.H','it.MCQ.L','it.HH.F','it.D')]) - means of facet means on the 1-5 agree scale. In study3-maindat.csv they are non-integer in 144/156 rows each (ranges 2.2-5 and 2.6-5); the do-file rounds them into resp 2-5 and 3-5. No wording exists; they ship in their own section_id (_2) with item_text, section_prompt and option_text blank, resp rows 1-5, so the item set still matches the live table. DATA DEFECT 2 (averaged informants): study3-maindat.csv is one row per target, and each it.* adjective value is the mean over that target's informants (325 informants on 156 targets). 1628 of 4546 non-missing adjective cells (35.8%) are non-integer (e.g. 5.5, 7.5); data/sun_2025_morality.do does `replace resp = round(resp)`. So live resp is a rounded per-target mean, not one respondent's choice of a scale point. The same applies to every Study 3 it.* table built from this file. Rights: the adjective battery is the study's own; no instrument rights holder or restriction applies.
public_note: Item text for the 30 adjectives is the study codebook's wording for the nominator form of the same battery (the informant-form stem is not separately published); itkindness and itintegrity are composite scores (means of the benevolence/respectfulness and honesty/loyalty/fairness/dependability facet means), not items, and carry no text; and every resp in this table is a per-target mean across informants rounded to an integer (35.8% of adjective values were non-integer before rounding), not a single rater's response.

note: WORDS: instructions and item_text are the Qualtrics header-row labels (row 2) of polarization_9 and polarization_10 in the study's own deposited export perceiver_ratings_raw_data.csv (OSF rf9k8 'Study 2 - Perceived Lifestyle Polarization/Data', osf.io/download/zhynf, sha256 8365d20afb6c8287b377f89c98aea04c9082198f8cfb066a51c73f1f70f8ef0e; same file the sibling talaifar_2025_study2_plp used). Each label is '<shared block prompt> - How would you rate conservatives?' / '... liberals?'; the shared prompt (identical in both labels) is shipped once as instructions and the part after ' - ' as item_text. Cross-checked against the survey printout in Supporting Text H of the APA supplement (supp.apa.org/psycarticles/supplemental/pspp0000545/pspp0000545.docx, sha256 8af3cba5d1f08192fe87f729c9ba3de5b5985768bf769f5cd327a68c75391e1d): prompt and both stems identical, stems numbered (9)/(10) matching QID24_9/QID24_10. Anchors: the printout's slider labels Cold/Neutral/Warm sit over ticks 0/50/100, shipped as option_text for resp 0/50/100; all other levels (0-100 slider) have no label and ship with option_text blank, not padded. Each item carries a row for every resp level its own respondents used plus the three anchor levels (conservative 59 rows, liberal 57; union = all 85 live levels). MAPPING: IRW codes come from a hand-written rename in data/talaifar_2025_lifestyle_polarization.py (polarization_9->conservative, polarization_10->liberal); the codes are self-describing and agree with their own labels. Checked anyway after applying the script's filters (156 respondents): live 'conservative' equals polarization_9 for 156/156 respondents (vs 23/156 against polarization_10), live 'liberal' equals polarization_10 for 156/156 (vs 23/156); means 38.80 and 61.19 reproduce. DEVIATIONS: Qualtrics label line breaks and tabs (\n\n\t) collapsed to single spaces; the prompt's reference to 'Democrats and Republicans' while the items name conservatives and liberals is the source's own wording, kept verbatim. RIGHTS: feeling-thermometer wording is ANES-style; instrument_rights_register.csv carries an ANES/NES 'ship' verdict (2026-09-16 email permission, covering question wording) which is applied here, not re-derived; the study's own Qualtrics text is deposited under CC BY-SA 4.0 (OSF rf9k8 node licence) with no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause located. SOURCE-RECORD DEFECT: dictionary DOI 10.1037/pspp0000549 resolves (Crossref, 2026-09-23) to a different article (title 'Methods reflect values: Evaluating the shortcomings of the average...', JPSP 128:1355-1370); the correct DOI is 10.1037/pspp0000545 (Crossref title 'Lifestyle polarization on a college campus...', 129:152-180).
public_note: The prompt respondents read says 'We would like to get your feelings toward both Democrats and Republicans', but the two items actually ask for ratings of conservatives and liberals; the wording is reproduced as administered.
